title: Schemathematics

hero.headline: What does the object do?
hero.support: Schemathematics studies how formal structures are represented, differentiated, composed, transformed, and made intelligible across schemas. It treats the schema itself as a consequential mathematical carrier rather than as passive notation.

definition.title: A schema should tell you what structure is available and what operations it licenses.
definition.body: Schemathematics is the formal study of schemas as lawful generators and carriers of objects, transformations, admissibility conditions, invariants, defects, provenance, and repair.
definition.discipline: Prefer established mathematics wherever it already carries the required structure. The research question is whether an explicit operative atlas across those structures improves comparison, navigation, translation, pedagogy, or machine reasoning.

operativeProfile.title: Profile the object by operation, not by name alone.

fields.name: Entity
fields.question: What kind of object is being represented?

fields.name: Admissibility
fields.question: What conditions must hold before the object or operation is well-formed?

fields.name: Transformations
fields.question: Which maps, actions, or rewrites are lawful?

fields.name: Invariants
fields.question: What must survive those lawful transformations?

fields.name: Closure
fields.question: Which operations remain inside the represented structure?

fields.name: Boundary
fields.question: Which added or removed condition changes the object's available behavior?

fields.name: Provenance
fields.question: Which prior distinctions or constructions are required to reconstruct the object?

fields.name: Defect / repair
fields.question: What fails when a required condition is omitted, and what restores the intended structure?

coreQuestions: What structure must exist for this object to do what it does?
Which distinction does the object introduce?
What remains invariant across equivalent or alternative representations?
Which dependency edges are required to reconstruct the object without hidden jumps?
What does one representation expose that another suppresses or makes expensive?

program.representation: Express formal objects through typed operative profiles rather than names alone.
program.comparison: Compare neighboring structures by the constraints, transformations, and invariants that differentiate them.
program.composition: Study when local schemas compose lawfully and where hidden loss appears at interfaces.
program.transport: Track what survives admissible movement between representations.
program.computation: Test whether structured schema representations improve mathematical navigation, derivation, discrimination, and machine reasoning.
program.pedagogy: Treat unexplained conceptual jumps as candidate missing dependency edges rather than as unavoidable abstraction.

workedExample.title: Worked comparison: monoid → group.
workedExample.purpose: This is intentionally established mathematics. The test is whether operative profiling makes the structural difference easier to see without inventing a new object.

monoid.entity: A set M equipped with a binary operation.
admissibility: the operation maps M × M back into M
there is an identity element e
guaranteedOperations: compose any finite sequence of elements
insert or remove the identity without changing the result
notGuaranteed: solving a · x = b or x · a = b inside M for arbitrary a and b

group.entity: A monoid in which every element has an inverse.
group.addedCondition: For every a in G there exists a⁻¹ in G with a·a⁻¹ = a⁻¹·a = e.
newlyGuaranteed: reversible multiplication by any group element
unique solutions to a · x = b and x · a = b inside the group

workedExample.boundaryDistinction: The promotion from monoid to group is the addition of universal invertibility. That one condition changes which transformations are guaranteed reversible and which equations are guaranteed solvable inside the structure.
workedExample.schemaLesson: The names are useful labels; the operative profile exposes why the distinction matters. A useful schema should let a reader recover the added condition, the new guarantees it licenses, and the operations that remain unavailable without it.

validation.title: The program succeeds only if the representation earns its cost.
tests: Formal fidelity: preserve accepted definitions and required conditions.
Differentiating power: make neighboring structures easier to distinguish.
Dependency clarity: expose which prior distinctions are required.
Transformational utility: show which operations and invariants become available.
Pedagogical transfer: allow reconstruction without hidden conceptual jumps.
Equivalence burden: reduce to established formal machinery when that machinery already carries the required structure.
validation.comparisonShape: Compare conventional name/definition lookup with operative-profile representations on bounded tasks such as structure discrimination, prerequisite reconstruction, operation selection, and cross-representation translation.
validation.claimRule: Any claimed improvement in theorem proving, retrieval, pedagogy, or mathematical AI requires benchmark evidence beyond illustrative examples.

researchHypotheses: Formal objects can be indexed by operative profiles containing entity type, admissibility conditions, lawful transformations, invariants, closure properties, provenance, and boundary structure.
Operationally equivalent representations may remain asymmetric in visibility, cognitive cost, and computational usefulness.
Cross-domain discovery may improve when objects are matched by operative profile rather than terminology alone.
Structured Schemathematics representations may improve mathematical navigation and reasoning relative to vector-only retrieval, but this remains an empirical hypothesis.

claimBoundary.title: Formal research framing, not a novelty claim by default.
safe: Schemathematics is a current Boundary First Labs research framing and formalization program.
Its objects and hypotheses can be tested independently of Boundary Theory as a whole.
Existing category theory, type theory, topology, algebra, logic, formal methods, knowledge representation, and related mathematics must be imported where they already solve the problem.
The monoid/group example demonstrates the representation method using standard mathematics; it is not evidence that the underlying algebra is new.
notYetEstablished: that Schemathematics is a new mathematical field in the priority sense
that it improves theorem proving or mathematical AI without benchmark evidence
that operative profiles outperform established mathematical notation across tasks
that any proposed Boundary First primitive is necessary when an established formalism is sufficient

closing.title: Make the difference between objects reconstructable, not merely nameable.
closing.finalLine: Represent the conditions. Expose the operations. Compare the boundary. Preserve what established mathematics already knows.

notes: Current canon: Schemathematics powers Representational Mechanics and sits within the formal apparatus of Boundary Theory.
Public page should foreground comparison, formal fidelity, and falsifiability rather than novelty claims.
Source basis includes the Schemathematics Atlas first pass and Research Deployment Packet.
